variants.headline: Looking back: party leader faces a public scandal
variants.sub: A party leader is the subject of a newly revealed scandal.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: A scandal concerning a party leader had come to light in {colony}.

A leader, a scandal, and a story everyone can be tempted to improve in the telling. Resist the temptation. The revelation is news enough. Readers deserve a sharp question about trust, not a collection of invented details dressed up as the delicious part of the story.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

This paper treats {target} as a subject for scrutiny, while withholding conclusions the reported revelation does not establish. Attention to trust need not depend upon an invented account of wrongdoing.
